title: Roles, checks and fair sharing of the group's money

say: Roles, checks, and fair sharing of the group's money.
This is the video for module two of Cooperative and Group Enterprise Management.

In many groups, important tasks belong to everybody, which means nobody. Or one energetic member takes the order, collects the deposit, buys materials and keeps the records alone. Even if she is honest, the group cannot see what happened, and suspicion grows.

panel.heading: Everybody's job is nobody's job
items: Give every task one named owner
Split every money process between two
Check quality and the bank every month
Share surplus by a written rule

say: Separation of duties fixes this. Every money process is split between at least two people, so an error by one is likely to be noticed by another.
It is not an accusation. It protects an honest treasurer, because the records show what happened.

say: A standard operating procedure, or SOP, is a one-page list of steps with an owner for each. For example, Hauwa's catering cooperative in Kaduna gets an order for 200 plates at 3,500 naira a plate. Aisha, the sales lead, sends a written quote for 700,000 naira.

panel.heading: Hauwa's catering order, step by step
items: Sales lead sends a written quote
Deposit into the group account only
Treasurer confirms the payment
Bookkeeper records it with the reference
Production delivers, balance paid, receipt

say: The customer pays a 60 percent deposit of 420,000 naira into the cooperative's bank account. Aisha never accepts it into her own account.

panel.rule: Customer money never goes into a personal account.

say: If your group cooks or processes food, add hygiene to the SOP. These follow the WHO Five Keys to Safer Food. Wash hands with soap and clean water. Separate raw and cooked foods. Cook thoroughly, and keep food at safe temperatures.
A member with diarrhoea or vomiting should not handle food that day.

panel.heading: Food orders: hygiene in the SOP
items: Wash hands with soap and clean water
Separate raw and cooked foods
Cook thoroughly
Keep food at safe temperatures
Sick members do not handle food

say: A buyer expects the same quality whoever made the item. So write a specification sheet clear enough that two members checking one item reach the same verdict. Then inspect each batch and record the results.
Never criticise weak work publicly on WhatsApp.

panel.heading: When work falls short
left: Post faults in the group chat
right: Name the fault, set a date
Pair her with a stronger member

say: Return faulty pieces privately, with the fault named, for example hem uneven by 2 cm, and a date to correct it. If she fails twice, pair her with a stronger member.

say: Every month, compare the cashbook balance with the bank statement for the same date, and explain every difference.
For example, Grace in Jos found the cashbook at 412,500 naira and the bank at 389,000. First, bank charges and SMS fees of 1,500 naira were missing.

panel.heading: Make the cashbook match the bank
items: Bank charges not yet recorded
Payments that reached the bank unrecorded
Deposits the bank shows the next day
Mistakes, such as a line written twice

say: A member's 20,000 naira share payment was never written down, and a 45,000 naira deposit showed at the bank a day later.

say: The last 3,000 naira was a thread payment written twice. Both sides then showed 434,000 naira, and two people signed.
If money is still missing, do not accuse anyone in the group chat. The supervisory committee asks privately and reports to the general meeting.

say: Now cost an order. Members' labour is a real cost. If the price only covers materials, members are working for nothing.
The order is worth 1,950,000 naira. Materials cost 855,000, and sewing labour paid to members is 450,000. With cutting, transport, fuel and bank fees, total costs come to 1,470,000 naira.
That leaves a surplus of 480,000 naira.
Capacity check: 30 sets a day means 10 days, plus a 20 percent buffer is 12 days. That fits the 15-day deadline, so they accept.
Share the surplus by the rule in your bylaws. In this example, 25 percent, 120,000 naira, goes to the reserve.

cards.d: 336,000 naira, or 1,120 naira for each set a member sewed.

say: 5 percent, 24,000 naira, goes to training.

cards.d: 336,000 naira, or 1,120 naira for each set a member sewed.

say: And 70 percent is a patronage refund, shared by how much each member did: 1,120 naira per set. Bisola sewed 70 sets and gets 78,400 naira. Shade sewed 30 and gets 33,600.
Share only after the customer has paid in full, and never change the rule after the figures are known.

cards.d: 336,000 naira, or 1,120 naira for each set a member sewed.

say: To remember. Give every task one owner. Split every money process between two people. Reconcile with the bank monthly. And count members' labour as a cost before you share any surplus by the written rule.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One named owner for every task
Two people in every money process
Reconcile with the bank every month
Labour is a cost; share surplus by the rule
